_comment: Canonical source of truth for SSL certificate pins. Each domain pins ONLY the ROOT CA SPKI hashes of every CA that can issue its certificate. Roots are the only durable pin target: leaves are re-keyed on every renewal and every CA in play issues from a rotating pool of intermediates - both have already broken leaf/intermediate pins in production (2026-07-07 Let's Encrypt -> GTS edge rotation, 2026-07 Amazon M01 -> M04 intermediate rotation). Hashes are base64-encoded SHA-256 of the Subject Public Key Info, derived from the root certificates that scripts/generateCertificatePins.sh downloads and verifies against the SHA-256 fingerprints committed in its ROOT_MANIFEST (a TLS server never sends its root, so pins cannot be read off a live handshake). Regenerate with scripts/generateCertificatePins.sh; use --verify to confirm live chains anchor at a pinned root. Cloudflare-fronted hosts pin the roots of every CA Cloudflare can issue from - Let's Encrypt, Google Trust Services, SSL.com, and Sectigo (its backup-certificate CA, deployed automatically on a revocation or key compromise); GTS Root R2 is not pinned because Mozilla removed it from its root store in 2026. Native code (Android network_security_config_enforce.xml, CertificatePinning.kt, react-native-nitro-fetch Cronet patch, iOS CertificatePinning.swift, and the Mobile-Expensify HybridApp equivalents) MUST be kept in sync with this file; tests/unit/generateCertificatePinsTest.ts checks that the script output, this file and the native files agree.
